 With prices starting at just $4. This content is reviewed by the 7NEWS Editorial team. 7NEWS may receive a commission when you buy from links on our site. Prices correct at time of publication.
 By Ariana Pezeshki Beauty shopping can become expensive rather quickly.
 But some of the products making their way into Australian shopping trolleys come with surprisingly small price tags.
 Priceline’s best-sellers offer a snapshot of the beauty buys shoppers are reaching for across sunscreen, skincare, makeup, lips, haircare and fragrance.
 Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today Arrow 
 The line-up includes a $4 lip gloss, a $9.50 skincare serum and a facial sunscreen designed for everyday wear. 
 Whether you’re restocking the bathroom cabinet or looking for something new to try, these six products are worth a closer look.
 Sunscreen: La Roche-Posay Anthelios Invisible Fluid SPF 50+ 50mL, $40.99. Credit: Priceline 1. Sunscreen: La Roche-Posay Anthelios Invisible Fluid SPF 50+ 50mL, $40.99
 Sunscreen remains an everyday skincare essential, and La Roche-Posay Anthelios Invisible Fluid SPF 50+ is designed to slot into a daily routine without leaving a heavy finish.
 Priced at $40.99, the fragrance-free facial sunscreen offers very high UVA and UVB protection and has been formulated for sensitive skin. Its lightweight fluid texture is designed to leave an invisible finish, making it an option for those who like to apply makeup over their sunscreen.
 The formula is non-comedogenic, meaning it is designed not to clog pores, and has undergone dermatological and ophthalmological testing.
 Be the first to know: Add 7NEWS as your preferred news source on Google For those who prefer a different texture, the brand also offers other facial sunscreen options, including formulas designed for oily or dry skin.
 Always read the label and follow the directions for use. Sunscreen is only one component of sun protection. Wear protective clothing, a hat and sunglasses, seek shade and avoid excessive sun exposure.
 Skincare: The Ordinary Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1% 30mL, $9.50. Credit: Priceline 2. Skincare: The Ordinary Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1% 30mL, $9.50
 At $9.50, The Ordinary Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1% Serum is an accessible addition to a skincare routine for those interested in managing the appearance of uneven texture and excess oil.
 The water-based serum combines niacinamide, a form of vitamin B3, with zinc PCA. It is designed to improve the appearance of skin texture, boost radiance and minimise the appearance of pores.
 The brand also cites clinical testing involving 35 participants , with results reported after consistent use. However, individual results will vary, and skincare outcomes depend on a range of factors.
 For beauty shoppers who enjoy experimenting with their routines without committing to a hefty price tag, this one could be an appealing starting point.
 Lips: Essence Extreme Shine Volume Lipgloss 02 Summer Punch 5mL, $4. Credit: Priceline 3. Lips: Essence Extreme Shine Volume Lipgloss 02 Summer Punch 5mL, $4
 A glossy lip can pull together a makeup look, and Essence Extreme Shine Volume Lipgloss in Summer Punch costs just $4.
 The lip gloss delivers a high-shine, wet-look finish with a non-sticky texture. The range includes different finishes and effects, from radiant shine to plumping styles, depending on the product selected.
 The formula is vegan and free from added silicones, oil and microplastic particles, according to the product information supplied.
 Makeup: L’Oréal Paris Infallible 3-Second Setting Mist 75mL, $30.99. Credit: Priceline 4. Makeup: L’Oréal Paris Infallible 3-Second Setting Mist 75mL, $30.99
 Anyone who has spent time perfecting their makeup before a long day will understand the appeal of a setting spray.
 The L’Oréal Paris Infallible 3-Second Setting Mist, priced at $30.99 , is designed to help extend makeup wear, with the brand claiming results of up to 36 hours.
 Its aerosol micro-diffusion system delivers a fine mist designed to dry quickly and distribute evenly across the face.
 L’Oréal Paris also describes the formula as transfer-resistant, waterproof, heat-proof and sweat-proof. These are manufacturer claims, rather than a guarantee of performance in every condition.
 For those who like their makeup to stay in place from morning plans through to evening catch-ups, the setting mist is one to have on the radar.
 Haircare: Bouf Flouf Factor Growth Tonic 50mL, $34.95. Credit: Priceline 5. Haircare: Bouf Flouf Factor Growth Tonic 50mL, $34.95
 Haircare has become another area of interest for beauty shoppers, and Bouf Flouf Factor Growth Tonic is priced at $34.95 for 50mL. 
 The brand says its non-greasy formula uses its patented FGF5 hair technology and is designed to nourish the scalp, improve hair resilience and support thicker-looking strands.
 Bouf recommends applying the tonic twice daily for a minimum of three months for its suggested thickening results.
 As with any haircare product marketed for growth or density, results can vary. Claims about hair growth should be considered in light of the available evidence, and persistent or sudden hair loss is worth discussing with a qualified health professional.
 Fragrance: Guess Bella Vita EDP 100mL, $59. Credit: Priceline 6. Fragrance: Guess Bella Vita EDP 100mL, $59
 For shoppers who prefer their beauty purchases to come with a little sensory appeal, G uess Bella Vita Eau de Parfum is the fragrance pick in the line-up.
 The 100mL bottle is priced at $59 and features a fruity floral oriental fragrance profile, with top notes of black cherry, tuberose and tonka bean.
 The scent is designed to capture a feminine, sensual character, making it an option for those who enjoy richer, fruit-led fragrances.
 From an everyday sunscreen to a glossy $4 lip gloss, Priceline’s best-sellers span a range of budgets and beauty routines.
 Priceline’s best-sellers include the La Roche-Posay Anthelios Invisible Fluid SPF 50+, an everyday facial sunscreen priced at $40.99. Credit: Priceline And while a popular product isn’t automatically the right one for everyone, this list offers a useful starting point for anyone planning their next beauty restock.
 Priceline Pharmacy sales data collected between January — August 2026.
